stem: Per Rule 160101, are officers generally entitled to compensation from public funds for loss of private property in circumstances arising outside of their service?

options.A: Yes, in full, regardless of the circumstances of the loss
options.B: Yes, provided the loss occurred within Nigeria
options.C: No -- and officers may consider insuring their own property against loss or damage instead
options.D: Yes, but only up to 50% of the property's value

explanation: Rule 160101: officers will not, in general, be entitled to compensation from public funds for loss of property arising outside their service; officers may consider insuring their property instead.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 160201, where an officer dies in active service, what is paid to their legal representative or designated Next of Kin?

options.A: A one-time discretionary gift determined by the Permanent Secretary
options.B: Only the officer's final month's unpaid salary
options.C: Nothing, unless the death occurred while on official duty travel
options.D: Their entitlements under the life insurance policy maintained under Section 8 of the Pension Reform Act, 2014

explanation: Rule 160201: where an Officer dies in active service, the legal representative or designated Next of Kin is paid entitlements under the life insurance policy maintained under Section 8 of the Pension Reform Act, 2014.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 160202(a), if an officer's private vehicle is damaged as a direct result of civil disturbance while being used for official duties, who accepts responsibility?

options.B: No one -- civil disturbance damage is explicitly excluded from any compensation
options.C: The officer's private insurer exclusively, with no Government involvement

explanation: Rule 160202(a): if the Officer's private vehicle, whilst being used for official duties, is damaged as a direct result of civil disturbances, Government will accept responsibility for such damage.

stem: Per Rule 160202(a), does 'official duties' for this purpose include the officer's ordinary journey between house and office?

options.A: Yes -- 'Official duties' is deemed to include journeys between house and office
options.B: Only for officers on GL.15 and above
options.C: Only if the officer has no other means of transport
options.D: No, only formally assigned duty travel counts as official duties

explanation: Rule 160202(a): for the purpose of this Rule, 'Official duties' will be deemed to include journeys between house and office.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 160202(b), if an officer's private vehicle is damaged beyond repair in an accident during official duties, to what extent does Government accept responsibility?

options.A: Government accepts no responsibility in accident cases, only civil-disturbance cases
options.B: The difference between the indemnity covered by the insurance and the cost of replacing the vehicle
options.C: The full replacement cost of the vehicle, with no reference to the insurance indemnity
options.D: Half of the vehicle's original purchase price

explanation: Rule 160202(b): Government shall accept responsibility to the extent of the difference between the indemnity covered by the insurance and the cost of replacing the vehicle.

stem: Per Rule 160203(a), how long after an officer is declared missing must they remain not found before a Board of Enquiry is set up?
explanation: Rule 160203(a): where an Officer is reported missing and is not found within a period of one year from the date declared missing, a Board of Enquiry shall be set up.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 160203(b), once a missing officer is presumed dead, what is the Next of Kin entitled to?

options.A: Only the Officer's outstanding unpaid salary for the final month
options.B: Death benefit under the Group Life Assurance Scheme (GLA) and the total amount accrued to the Officer's Retirement Savings Account
options.C: Only a one-time cash gift of unspecified amount
options.D: Nothing, until the officer's body is formally recovered

explanation: Rule 160203(b): the Next-of-Kin shall be entitled to death benefit under the GLA and the total amount accrued to the Officer's Retirement Savings Account.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 160204, who pays the premium for the free health insurance cover an officer enjoys on official assignment outside Nigeria?

options.A: The officer's private insurer, with no Government involvement
options.C: The officer themselves, with later reimbursement

explanation: Rule 160204: an Officer on official assignment outside Nigeria shall enjoy free health insurance cover for the duration of the assignment, with the premium at Government expense.

stem: Per Rule 160205, who is responsible for arranging insurance during a stop-over en route to an officer's approved destination abroad?

options.A: Government, at full expense, identical to coverage at the final destination
options.B: The Nigerian Mission in the stop-over country
options.C: No insurance arrangement is required for a stop-over
options.D: The Officer themselves, making their own arrangements

explanation: Rule 160205: officers who make stop-over en route to an approved destination shall make their own arrangements for insurance from the place of stop-over.

stem: Per Rule 160206, under which Act is compensation for fatal cases or injury in a workplace (or outside it) treated?
explanation: Rule 160206: compensation in fatal cases/injury in a work place or outside the normal working place shall be treated as provided for in the Employees' Compensation Act 2010.

stem: Per Rule 160206, within how long after the incident must compensation payment for a fatal case or injury be made?
explanation: Rule 160206: payment shall be within three months after the incidence.
